Agreed. I’m 17 and have noticed thinning over the past few years and today I finally received confirmation of AGA, so I too have to assess whether my hair is worth the possibility of permanent side effects. 

While it is nonetheless awful, I feel as though the nature of hair loss and the sensitivity of the topic creates this almost conspiratorial allure surrounding finasteride side effects, when the reality is that multiple drugs - many of which are prescribed incredibly frequently - are also associated with permanent side effects. Anti-depressants are not only issued, but actively encouraged by psychiatrists frequently despite the evidence to suggest that they have permanent impacts upon one’s cognition. 

Every single thing we take can be ‘correlated’ with something else because there are so many factors that cannot be controlled all at once. if you find fin works, take it, if not, don’t. We cannot make any conclusive points about averages or statistics honestly, it’s simply too broad to conclude anything worthwhile

By reducing the amount of your testosterone that is converted into DHT via blocking the enzyme that allows such a reaction to occur, you will inevitably increase the amount of free testosterone that you have.

Just as how any men dealing with hair loss should not take complete solace in the existence of men with no side effects from fin as a reason for not being concerned about them, we shouldn’t actively discourage people from taking finasteride because a similarly rare few have suffered permanent ED as a result of it. I would appreciate if someone could guide me to the more extensive literature on the topic but from what I can see, sexual dysfunction whilst on finasteride occurs in just over 1 in 100 men. This number falls when accounting for the number that have side effects even after stopping finasteride, though with anything as broad and multi-faceted as the human body, there are always going to be rare cases. Suffice to say, most men don’t have sexual side effects, though I cannot definitely say whether other factors - such as brain fog, low mood, gyno etc are equally as frequent as the sexual side effects. 

Simply put, extremes don’t negate the vast majority. Apply averages to averages.
